actions.description: Set the seed used by the simulated world's random number generators for subsequent steps, without resetting the world. The accepted seed is echoed in the receipt.

facts.text: The gym environment explorer-v01 is registered with entry point mars_explorer.envs:Explorer
The action space is Discrete(4): four integer actions 0, 1, 2 and 3
The observation space is a Box with minimum 0 and maximum 1
The default map is 21 by 21 cells
Action 0 moves one cell on the first axis, action 1 the opposite way, action 2 one cell on the second axis and action 3 the opposite way
A move outside the map sets out_of_bounds and a move into an obstacle sets collision
The step reward is the number of newly explored cells minus the movement cost
The default movement cost is 0.2
The episode ends when timeStep is greater than max_steps
The default max_steps is 400
The episode ends with bonus_reward when more than 95 percent of the map is explored
The default bonus_reward is 400
A collision or an out-of-bounds move ends the episode with collision_reward or out_of_bounds_reward
The default collision_reward and out_of_bounds_reward are -400
The lidar scans 32 channels with a range of 6 cells
The default initial position is [0, 0]
The default configuration places 12 obstacles with margins [1, 1] and obstacle size [2, 2]
reset() takes no arguments and returns the initial observation
step() returns the legacy four-tuple (observation, reward, done, info)
reset() has no seed parameter and the class defines no seed() method
Obstacle positions are drawn with numpy's global random generator (np.random.randint)
The lidar resolution default is 200 samples

determinism.notes: The map generator draws obstacle positions and sizes from numpy's global RNG (randomMapGenerator.py:71-72) and Explorer.reset() takes no seed (explorer.py:38); cap.world.seed.v1 records a seed for the next reset but the upstream environment does not consume it, so two resets do not repeat a trajectory.

gaps: kinematic grid world only: one step is one discrete move to a neighbouring cell, with no forces, velocities, contacts, actuator, sensor or noise dynamics (fidelity level F0)
the map and lidar come from numpy's global RNG and reset() accepts no seed; reset is stochastic and cap.world.seed.v1 is not consumed by the upstream environment
no wall-clock pacing and no fixed timestep: one step is one control transition, so timestep_ms is 0 (an event-driven analytic model)

the package's fake re-implements the map generator, lidar, reward and terminal rules in pure Python without numpy or pygame; it was not compared with the upstream environment and its random stream differs from numpy's
the bridge flattens the 21 x 21 x 1 observation array to 441 numbers in the JSON observation; cap.world.render.v1 is not bound and the pygame viewer is not modelled
no physical device is modelled and the model was never validated against one

measures.description: Last observation (derived from the observation space)
measures.name: observation

safe_state.description: the simulation stops advancing: no step or reset is accepted after an e-stop until mhs.safety.reset clears the latch; the last observation and grid state are kept and stay readable
